expectations.text: Diagnoses that $var.<childJobId>.job_details may not resolve inside query.obj on some platform versions
expectations.evidence: Transcript final answer states: 'Root cause: The job_details output of a childJob task is a special object that on some platform builds is not resolved as a live object reference when referenced directly as a $var string ("obj": "$var.<childJobId>.job_details") inside a downstream query task's incoming.obj. Instead, on those versions the platform stores/reads it as a literal string.' The output JSON's _notes array repeats this diagnosis verbatim. This matches the skill's own documented gotcha at SKILL.md line 367 ('check whether "obj": "$var.<childJobId>.job_details" is resolving — on some platform versions it is treated as a literal string') and line 669, confirming the diagnosis is grounded in the actual skill content, not invented.

suggestions.assertion: Provides the merge+taskRef workaround: merge data_to_merge includes {'task': childJobId, 'variable': 'job_details'}
suggestions.reason: This assertion is easy to satisfy by copy-pasting the exact SKILL.md example verbatim (which is what happened here) — it doesn't discriminate between an executor that actually understood why the workaround works versus one that pattern-matched the literal JSON snippet from the skill file. Consider adding a check that the explanation also covers *why* taskRefs resolve reliably while $var strings don't (which this run did include unprompted), so future runs that only copy the JSON without explaining the mechanism are caught.

No assertion checks whether the agent flags the second, unrelated failure mode (child workflow not explicitly setting taskStatus) that produces an identical symptom. This run caught it unprompted and it materially improves the debugging advice (a user could burn time on the merge fix when the real problem is on the child side) — a good discriminating assertion would check this since a shallow response would only address the platform-quirk half of the story.

eval_feedback.overall: All four expectations pass with genuine, verifiable grounding — the transcript's quoted SKILL.md excerpts and the output JSON's task wiring were independently checked against the actual SKILL.md file and asset JSON files and match near-verbatim (including exact line numbers and gotcha numbering). The one inaccuracy found (claiming 'every' childJob instance uses loopType: "" when one uses 'sequential') is minor and doesn't affect the core diagnosis or fix. Evals could be strengthened by adding an assertion around the child-workflow-side taskStatus sanity check, since that was a genuine value-add this run produced that no current expectation rewards or would catch if omitted.
